Subject: NovaCorp TCO follow-up & next steps

Alex —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through the NovaCorp inference use case. Quick recap of the pain, goals, and the cost levers we discussed so the team has a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- High per-request cost for contextualized responses (long history + high QPS).
- Latency spikes during peak traffic windows (~2–3x baseline).
- Difficulty forecasting monthly inference spend (seasonal campaigns).

Goals & success metrics:
- Reduce per-token cost by ~30% while keeping P99 latency under 200ms for interactive calls.
- Predictable monthly spend with a <=10% variance target.
- Demonstrate 3-month ROI on the search/chat pilot.

Primary cost levers we recommended (high-level):
1) Batching: group near-concurrent requests into micro-batches. For your QPS profile (avg 250 qps, 1.2k burst) we estimate a 15–25% cost reduction with conservative batching and minimal latency impact.
2) KV/prefix caching: cache repeated context blocks (common prompts and user history snippets). For NovaCorp's session reuse patterns this could save an additional 20–30% on tokens processed.
3) Model & precision tuning: using a 4-bit quantized variant for high-throughput routes and reserving the higher-precision model for escalations can drop unit costs ~20% vs float16 on the same hardware.
4) Dedicated capacity & pre-warm strategy: Reserving dedicated pools for campaign windows reduces variance and prevents costly burst throttles.

Preliminary TCO numbers (monthly, rough):
- Estimated tokens/month (production pilot): 1.2B prompt+completion tokens
- Baseline projected hosted cost (no optimization): $48k/mo
- With batching + caching + quantization + reserved capacity: $26k–30k/mo (~40–55% reduction)

Next steps / asks:
- We’ll share a short TCO workbook with assumptions (attached). Please confirm the monthly token estimate we used (1.2B) or share adjusted numbers.
- Rafael will follow up with a quick config recommendation (batch size, cache TTLs, quantization profile).
- If this looks good, we can scope a 6–8 week pilot (integration + pilot SLA + evaluation prompts).

Thanks again — happy to hop on a follow-up with your infra and procurement folks next week.

Best,

Hi all —

Quick configuration notes as promised. These are conservative starting points — happy to iterate once we get telemetry from your staging traffic.

Assumptions used for the estimate:
- Pilot traffic: 1.2B tokens/month (production scenario) and staggered scenario of 1.6B for campaign peak.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 equivalent on dedicated pools for interactive routes; larger batch workers for async jobs.
- Baseline model cost: $0.00004 per token (hosted, no optimizations) — this matches earlier benchmarking for your model family.

Recommended levers & expected impact:
1) Batching: target micro-batch window of 15–30ms, max batch size 32 for interactive. Effective per-token cost reduction ~18% at your QPS if we hit 60% batching efficiency.
2) KV caching: TTL 6h for session prefixes, cache hit target 25–30% on first pass. Expected token savings 22–28%.
3) Quantization: use q4_0 for the steady route, fallback to fp16 for edge cases — expected unit cost delta ~20% vs fp16.
4) Reserved pools & pre-warm: reserve 2–3 dedicated workers for peak windows; hard cap for burst to avoid autoscale losses. Operational overhead adds ~5% to baseline infra but stabilizes variance.

How the $26k–30k was derived (high-level):
- Start from baseline billed tokens: 1.2B tokens * $0.00004 = $48,000
- Apply batching (18%): ~$39,360
- Apply KV caching (25% effective on remaining): ~$29,520
- Apply quantization (20% on compute portion): ~$23,616
- Add reserved infra overhead and support (~5%): ~$24,800
- Allow variance and staging/ingestion costs => $26k–30k/mo range for conservative budgeting.

Attachments: I attached a short workbook with the line-by-line math and sensitivity (novacorp-tco-summary.xlsx).

Next steps I suggest:
- Alex/Priya: confirm whether we should model 1.2B or 1.6B tokens for the initial procurement ask.
- Marissa / Ben: draft SOW and MRR banding for procurement review; I'll help with technical appendix.
- Schedule Wed 6/23 10:00am PT to align on pilot scope and sign-off items.

Rafael
